issues.passage: The surplus dwindled after three consecutive quarters of record profits and expansion.
issues.why: Valid, natural use of dwindle (= diminish gradually). Expansion and post-profit spending often shrink a surplus; the verb is used correctly, so marking this wrong is a swap.

fix.correctPassage: As grant funding dwindled, the lab had to close two of its three field stations.
wrongPassages: Enrollment dwindled from forty students to several hundred within a single term.
The surplus dwindled as quarterly profits kept setting new highs and the reserve fund tripled.
Her confidence dwindled into a keynote that packed the largest auditorium on campus.
